diagnosis: All 4 rollouts fail the same two checks, C4 and C5, in the same way. In every rollout, PF2 is properly revealed by A3 and properly cited in justification_fact_ids, so the failure is not disclosure or provenance. The settlements all correctly set alternative_hospice_arranged_for to "Patient B" and all include a commitment to send the referral packet to Harbor Hospice today. The failure is ENCODING MISMATCH: C4 and C5 are checking for specific fields or exact strings that the settlements do not produce, even though the underlying information from PF2 is present and used. Specifically, the settlements encode the Harbor Hospice appointment time (13:00) and the packet-handoff commitment in the commitments array with free-text detail strings (e.g., "Send Patient B's referral packet to Harbor Hospice today to secure the intake appointment tomorrow at 13:00"), but C4 and C5 apparently expect either a dedicated decision field (e.g., a field capturing the exact 13:00 appointment time) or an exact commitment type/target string that the model never produces verbatim. The model naturally encodes the appointment time and the handoff as a follow-up commitment with a detail string, not as a separate structured field or a commitment with a specific type label. This is consistent across all 4 rollouts: rollouts 0 and 2 use commitment type "follow-up" or "send_referral_packet" with target "Patient B" or "Harbor Hospice"; rollouts 1 and 3 use "follow_up" or "referral_packet_submission" with target "Luis" or "Harbor Hospice". No rollout auto-failed on turn cap; all settled in 4-6 turns. No telepathy, no never-revealed, no revealed-but-unused, no misapplied — the group had the right information and used it correctly; the checks simply do not match the natural encoding.
